newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks fall in late trade on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks fall in late trade on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices fell in late Wednesday trade after a mixed opening as the recent bellwether sector electronics saw profit-taking intensify, but brokers said they saw support at 8,300 points.
With 62 minutes left, at 0258 GMT, the index was down 68.81 points or 0.82 percent at 8,324.17. Turnover was T$76 billion.
Electronics were down 1.85 percent, with leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor down T$3.5 to T$131.
Warrant-eligible shares rose to support the market, with Pacific Wire and Cable up 40 cents to T$41.3.
"Profit-taking on electronics is quite normal," said United Securities vice-president Lin Long-hsien.
"There are mixed viewpoints about the index's future trend," Lin said. "But I believe support at 8,300 is strong and a firming trend after a short period of consolidation is very likely."
